scope: Independent visual crosscheck of the three new noun patterns and selected adjective derivation rules. Does not claim an exhaustive linguistic review of all Unit9 lexical cells or later prose.

images.finding: Cook§43 full masculine model and diagnostic vowel/syncope conditions; supports shared-model derivation rather than a new arbitrary suffix rule.
Cook§43.6 explicitly gives agent nouns in -end with plural zero/-e (rare -as) and genitive plural -ra; the selected geðeahtend pattern follows this bounded rule.
Cook§45 prints sunu/suna/suna in the singular and suna/suna/sunum in the plural, plus precise documented variation. NGDA expansion includes both nominative and accusative cells.
Cook§48 begins the neuter-e model; the preceding §47 notes distinguish disyllabic retention/syncope from an unqualified stem-weight rule.
Cook§48 prints singular -e/-es/-e, plural -u/-a/-um; explicit rīcu/rīciu and rīca/rīcia alternatives are retained as variants.
Cook§57.3 describes disyllabic adjective endings and possible syncope, with lexical exceptions; §58 identifies long-monosyllable loss of -u.

Cook§59 prints strong grēne masculine/neuter and grēnu feminine, neuter plural grēnu/-e, and requires retention of lexical-e only where no ending is provided. This supports the source proposal's behēfu reference to the e-adjective pattern; §60 begins the weak declension.
